_about: Order, titles and lead lines of the report sections, and the list of sections a finding can be filed under. Builders read this file, so a section can be renamed or reordered here without touching code. A section that holds findings is left out when there are none (a Quick check has none).

questions.title: What the batch looks like
questions.ask: What does the work in these stories look like overall: places, activities, time?

questions.title: Repeat places
questions.ask: Does the same place appear in more than one story?

questions.title: How the idea spread
questions.ask: Did one village's work lead another village to ask for the same?

questions.title: Feelings and voice
questions.ask: What did community members feel, and is it in their own words?

questions.title: Why people chose the work
questions.ask: Why did people choose that work, and do the stories bring the reason out?

questions.title: What the stories leave out
questions.ask: What do the stories leave out, and what should writers be asked to include?

gaps.title: Women/men split of the people who worked
gaps.prompt: How many women and how many men took part in the work.

gaps.title: Who convened the meeting
gaps.prompt: Who called the meeting, who first suggested the work, and what the Goonj team did.

gaps.title: A result with a stated time gap
gaps.prompt: One result with a date and a number (people using it, time saved, produce).

gaps.title: An arrangement for looking after the work
gaps.prompt: Who will look after it, and how.

gaps.title: What families received (kit or materials) and when
gaps.prompt: What families received and when (kit contents, hand-over date).

gaps.title: Work dates (start and end)
gaps.prompt: Start date, end date, days worked, and the season.

gaps.title: Size of the work with a unit
gaps.prompt: Length, breadth and unit (or area) of what was built, repaired or planted.

gaps.title: Village, block and district all written
gaps.prompt: Village, block, district and state; distance from the main road.

gaps.title: A named resident's own words, with age
gaps.prompt: The problem in at least one named resident's own words, with age; keep the original-language text.

gaps.title: What people put in besides labour
gaps.prompt: What people put in besides labour (money, materials, tools, land, skills), with amounts.

gaps.title: A consent status where a named person gives a personal detail
gaps.prompt: A consent line for every named person who gives a personal detail.

gaps.title: A report or activity code
gaps.prompt: Report code or activity code (one field, one format).

gaps.title: Original-language text for the quotes
gaps.prompt: Keep the original-language text of every quote, next to the translation.

gaps.title: A photo in the file shared

writing_rules.text: Describe a result in the past tense only when a date or a visit shows it was seen.
Name a community only where a member of it speaks, and never from a surname.
Keep a quote to what was said; mark reported speech as reported.
If only women are counted, say whether any men took part.
Write the size of the work in one form, with its unit.

sections.title: In brief
sections.lead: Answers to the six questions this review was asked, in one place. Each points to the section with the evidence.

sections.title: The batch at a glance
sections.lead: Where the stories come from and what the work was.

sections.title: What each story is telling you
sections.lead: A reading of each story from its text alone: what the problem was, what people did, what the story shows about how the work came about, and what it leaves out. Names tied to a health, injury, bereavement or menstrual detail are held back.

sections.title: Who did the work
sections.lead: People who took part, as recorded. A women-only count is a minimum, not a total.

sections.title: Why people chose the work
sections.lead: The reason given, whose words it is in, and whether other needs were weighed.

sections.title: How Goonj came in and who decided
sections.lead: Who was at the meeting, who proposed the work, and whether the decision is shown or only stated.

sections.title: What people put in and who looks after it
sections.lead: Contributions beyond labour, and what the stories say about looking after the work.

sections.title: What changed, and how we know
sections.lead: Dates, results, evidence of change, and what went wrong.

sections.title: Feelings, voice and words
sections.lead: Who is quoted, how people felt, and whose words frame the work.

sections.title: Kit and Goonj's role
sections.lead: What the stories say about the exchange that defines the programme.

sections.title: The 19 Key Questions
sections.lead: Whether each story answers the questions the programme wants stories to answer. Clear means answered with specifics, partial means in general words, not stated means nothing answers it.

sections.title: What the stories leave out
sections.lead: Gaps counted across the batch. Each is a gap in the write-up, not necessarily in the village.

sections.title: Records, template and translation
sections.lead: What the stories carry as records, and what the template and the translation step do to them.

sections.title: Readiness for outside use
sections.lead: A 12-test checklist computed from the records, and a 1 to 5 band for each story.

sections.title: Sensitivity and consent
sections.lead: Named people, personal details and community labels.

sections.title: For the next stories
sections.lead: What to ask field writers to include, drawn from the gaps above.

sections.title: Questions for the writers
sections.lead: Plain, neutral and specific; no question assumes anything went wrong.

sections.title: How this was checked
sections.lead: What was done to make the numbers and findings reliable, and where they stop.
